# CC02: 含经堂 Hanjing Tang

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC02` · Page: `/scenes/CC02/` · Row: `research/buildings/CC02-hanjing-tang/`

## What it was

含经堂 Hanjing Tang, "Hall Holding the Classics", is the largest group of 长春园 Changchun Yuan, on the central island (E0494, E0057; Malone's No.2, E0056). The hall was new in 1747 (E0014, E0015, E0057). 日下旧闻考 Rixia Jiuwen Kao walks it from 云容水态 Yunrong Shuitai north-west by a hill path: three glazed 坊楔 arches, a five-bay south-facing gate, the seven-bay 含经堂, then 淳化轩 Chunhua Xuan (printed 淳化閣 in the list, 淳化軒 in the note) and 蕴真斋 Yunzhen Zhai on the axis, with 霞翥楼 Xiazhu Lou and 渊映斋 Yuanying Zhai to the east and 梵香楼 Fanxiang Lou and 涵光室 Hanguang Shi to the west (S05 j83:4a-4b; E0052). In 1770, his sixtieth year, Qianlong rebuilt the north part as the home he meant to retire to in the sixtieth year of his reign (E0401): he had the 淳化阁帖 recut and the slabs set in the existing galleries behind 含经堂, moved 蕴真斋 a little north and enlarged its old base into the hall 淳化轩 (S05 j83:5a-5b, E0051; E0055); 蕴真斋, 三友轩 Sanyou Xuan, 静莲斋 Jinglian Zhai, 待月楼 Daiyue Lou and 理心楼 Lixin Lou date from the same campaign (E0057). 霞翥楼, inner plaque 味腴书屋, was shelved for a set of the 四库全书荟要 (E0052, E0053, E0057); 梵香楼 opposite held some 700 Buddhist images (E0061). A shop street 买卖街 Maimai Jie ran outside the east wall (S940 p.360; E2156; S990). Like the rest of the gardens it was looted by French and British troops on 6-8 October 1860 and burned by British troops on Elgin's order on 18-19 October (S02 pp.179-188; S940 p.359); guards were still posted on the site after 1860 (E0057). The site was excavated in 2001-2003 (S990; E0062).

From the inventory row: **built** 乾隆十二年 1747 基本建成 (S43;S48); by c. 1747: first 含經堂 poem at the end of the first collection; by 1749 (poem 乾隆十四年); **changed** 1770-72 淳化轩 etc added (S43; S48; j83:5b, 6b); 1780 四库荟要 to 霞翥楼 (S48); 1814 theatre (S43;S48); 1770 rebuilt; 1814 stage east of 淳化轩; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S43, S48, S01, S201, S361).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Not one of the Forty Scenes of 1744.

### How later sources differ

The 1770 works changed the compound most: 淳化轩, 蕴真斋 and the west court with 三友轩 are of the 1770 campaign (E0057), and a note of 1771 says the galleries were done but the stones not yet carved (E0055). Jiaqing added a stage east of 淳化轩 in 1814 (E0057): the two-storey 乐奏钧天 Yuezou Juntian, facing the hall 神心妙达 Shenxin Miaoda, which was rebuilt in mid-Jiaqing as a five-bay viewing hall (S940 p.360). This fits the pasted slip of 1814 on the Yangshi Lei plan titled 长春园淳化轩, drawn after 1794 (E0060). Dated poems run on to 1810 at 含经堂 and to 1824 (Daoguang) at 淳化轩 (E0053, E0050, E0055). Malone repeats hearsay that Qianlong retired here after his abdication (E0056); the Qing texts read here record only the plan (E0401; S940 p.362).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

淳化轩: inner plaque 奉三无私, couplet 貞石麗延廊畧存古意 / 淳風扇寰宇冀遂初心, and the recut 淳化阁帖 stones set in the walls of the east and west galleries (S05 j83:4b; E0052). 蕴真斋: inner plaque 礼园书圃; 霞翥楼: inner plaque 味腴书屋, and the 四库全书荟要 on shelves fitted like those of 摛藻堂 in the palace (a note of 1777, E0053; E0052, E0057). 梵香楼: a Buddhist tower of some 700 images; a small bronze inscribed 地天母, found in the dig, is identified by the park's archaeologist as the only one known to survive (E0061).

### The garden around it

A forecourt south of the gate with three glazed arches on its east, south and west sides, crossing stone paths, carved-brick paving, foundations for yurts (毡帐) and planting pits; a Taihu-stone rockery in front of the 淳化轩 terrace; a piled-rock hill round 三友轩 in the west court (S990 contents; S940 p.360). Open halls on the water outside the walls: 澄波夕照 Chengbo Xizhao to the west and 得胜概 Desheng Gai behind the north gate (S940 p.360; S990; E0063). Malone's plate p.100 shows a rock garden north of it (E0056). Roofs come from S940, from texts and the ruin, not from a picture: 含经堂 a seven-bay double-eaved hip-and-gable hall (S940 p.360; S361 also calls it glazed, E0057), 淳化轩 hip-and-gable, rolled on p.360 and glazed on p.361, 渊映斋, 涵光室 and 静莲斋 five-bay hip-and-gable halls, and 待月楼 a three-bay hip-and-gable tower of two storeys (S940 p.360).

## What survives today

The whole 含经堂 compound was dug in 2001-03 by the 北京市文物研究所 team led by 靳枫毅 (S143; S990) and is shown as a consolidated ruin; the cleared site was presented by December 2003 (E0061). The brief's abstract, as reported in a library record, counts over 60,000 m2 of site, over 30,000 m2 of building remains and more than 30 building units (S143, E0062); the full report of 2006 describes every unit by name (S990). Measured on the ruin: 三友轩 11.1 x 7.2 m on a platform 11.9 x 8.3 m (S940 p.364). About twenty underfloor heating systems (地炕) survive with stokeholes, fireboxes and centipede-pattern flues; the largest stokehole, 2.37 x 1.8 m, is at 蕴真斋 (S940 pp.367-368). The stage 乐奏钧天 is about 16 m square over a granite cellar 2.47 m high (E0064, citing the brief). The shop row east of the wall left a base 135.65 m long, with 40 shop bays in 9 units and 28 stoves (E2156; S941, both citing S143); its width is given as about 6.3 m (E2156) and as about 63 m (S941), so it is open. The foundations of 澄波夕照, 得胜概 and a rock pavilion are reported to have been partly restored (E0063). The full brief and the 2006 report are not seen.

## Modern reconstructions, not evidence (6)

Never a source for a size or a position here.

Modern readings: the Tsinghua/清城睿现 AR guide (R0042), a model photograph and plan figures in 王文涛 Wang Wentao 2015 (R0316, R0317, S940), the dig drawings of S143/S990 (R0318) and, as a blog reports, a reconstruction board at the site (R0319). 王文涛 builds on the dig and the Yangshi Lei plan 长春园淳化轩 and compares 淳化轩 with 乐寿堂 Leshou Tang in the Forbidden City, which a Qing note says copied it (S940 p.362).

## The best views for modellers

For modellers: S990 (the full dig report, to request) and S940 (bays, roofs and one measured hall); the Yangshi Lei plan E0060 (catalogue record only, no image here); the excavated platforms on the 2013 photographs (P0403-P0410, P0505). 乐寿堂 in the 宁寿宫 Ningshou Gong, said by a Qing note to copy 淳化轩 (S940 p.362), is the nearest standing comparable for 淳化轩: a twin, not evidence for its size.

## Gaps and wishlist

No measured footprint of 含经堂, 淳化轩 or 蕴真斋 is on disk: they are in S990 chapter 3 and S143, neither seen. Roofs are stated only in S940 and S361, from texts and the ruin, and disagree for 淳化轩 (rolled or glazed); storeys are stated only for 待月楼 (two, S940 p.360); for 霞翥楼, 梵香楼 and 理心楼 two storeys are read from the name 楼 alone. The width of the shop street is open (6.3 or 63 m). The Yangshi Lei plan 样021-23 (E0060) is not viewed. No period picture: the compound is not in any album.

### Open questions that name it

- **Q9. Bay counts, plan against text.** They agree at 廓然大公, 蓬岛瑶台, 别有洞天, 观澜堂, 宫门, 远瀛观, 方外观. They differ: 澹怀堂 5 (plan, excavation via S112) vs 9 (S06); 含经堂 about 9 vs 7 (S05) vs 5 (S06); 正谊明道 about 8 vs 5 (S05) vs 7 (S48); 长春仙馆 7 vs 5; 茹古涵今 6 vs 5; 九洲清晏殿 5 vs 7; 勤政殿 4 vs 5; 上下天光 9 cells vs 3; 保合太和 9×3 vs 3; 鱼跃鸢飞 6×5 vs 5;
- **Q14. A label names which hall?** The readers found a working rule: a label in a court names the hall north of it (同顺堂, 含经堂, 澹怀堂 ...). Where halls stand on both sides it is an assumption. Applies to many `likely` rows.
- **Q45. Halls in the texts with no row.** 如园 CC18: 芝兰室, 云萝山馆, 听泉榭, 含碧楼, 挹霞亭, 观丰榭, 引胜轩 (S140). S360 names 无倦斋 (YM02), 万象涵春, 长春书屋, 池上居, 画禅室, 养正书屋 (YM03), 碧澜亭 (YM10), 得树亭 (YM09), 养素书屋 (YM04), 鸣玉溪, 春好轩 (YM12), 湛清华轩, 溜琴亭, 履吉斋, 晴望楼 (YM47), 纳翠轩, 翼翠亭 (YM48), 湛然室, 悦霁亭 (YM45), 水晶域 (YM20), 夏隐亭, 镜远洲 (YM31), 得趣书屋 (YM28), 活画舫 (YM34),
- **Q86. YM44-06 / CC02-15.** YM44-06 / CC02-15: two shop streets. Attiret's fair of 1743 (E2160) predates Changchun Yuan (c.1745-51), so his street is the 同乐园 one (YM44-06), as Malone p.94 says; the 含经堂 street CC02-15 (S115, E2156) is a later, separate street. Keep Attiret and Malone's 'New Year's Fair' caption on YM44-
- **Q108. CC02-10 三友轩.** CC02-10 三友轩: the ruin as measured (S940 p.364) is 11.1 x 7.2 m on a platform 11.9 x 8.3 m, but our row has frontage 14.8 m read off S01 (3x1 cells). Shrink the box to the measured size; check whether the plan cell scale in Changchun Yuan runs about 30% large for small halls. (digs worker, Round 7
- **Q109. CC02-15 买卖街.** CC02-15 买卖街: the dig brief (via S941) gives foundations 135.65 m N-S by about 63 m E-W, far more than our row (51 m frontage, 13x1 plan cells). Either the row covers only one wing of the street or the plan reading missed most units; check S01 east of the 含经堂 wall. (digs worker, Round 7)
- **Q143. CC02.** CC02: S361 (E0057) calls 含经堂 a double-eaved glazed hall; a search extract (unverified) says it was turned into a double-eaved hall in 1770. Grey or glazed tiles? The 2006 report S990 should say from tile finds; not seen. (w34 worker, Round 7)
- **Q151. CC02-04 淳化轩 roof.** CC02-04 淳化轩 roof: S672 p.360 says 卷棚歇山, p.361 says 琉璃歇山 (glazed hip-and-gable). Rolled or pointed ridge, grey or glazed? S990 tile finds should settle it. (w34 worker, Round 7)
- **Q156. Twin lead for the coordinator.** Twin lead for the coordinator: S672 p.362 quotes a Qing note (乐寿堂 entry: 长春园之淳化轩先已落成 ... 兹宁寿宫之乐寿堂，乃仿其规制为之) that 乐寿堂 in the 宁寿宫 copies 淳化轩 (CC02-04). 乐寿堂: seven by three bays, single-eaved hip-and-gable, yellow glazed tiles, 18.7 m from ground to ridge, columns removed in the fro
- **Q171. CC02.** CC02: S672 and S940 are the same paper (王文涛, 故宫学刊 2015, the same dpm.org.cn PDF). Merge the ids; the verified texts cite S940. (verify_b worker, Round 7)
- **Q172. CC02-15 买卖街.** CC02-15 买卖街: width of the shop street base disagrees: S941 (OCR of the 紫禁城 page) reads 东西宽约63米, E2156 (S115) gives about 6.3 m; both cite the dig brief S143. 40 bays in a row 135.65 m long fit 6.3 m better. Check the brief or the PDF image of S941 before any box. (verify_b worker, Round 7)
- **Q173. CC02-04 淳化轩.** CC02-04 淳化轩: S940 gives 卷棚歇山 (p.360) and 琉璃歇山 (p.361) for the same hall; only S361 (E0057) calls 含经堂 glazed. Tile finds in S990 should settle both. (verify_b worker, Round 7)
- **Q196. The width of a paved way 甬道 is not known anywhere.** No text and no published dig gives one; the drawn roads are 4-5 m (S01 at 大宫门 and 绮春园宫门); every other width is typology (`WIDTH` in `scripts/paths1860.py`). The digs of 含经堂 (S143, S990), 长春园宫门 (S316) and 大宫门 (S993) would.
